summary: Lincoln County, OR lookout near Waldport, built mid-1930s; cab or parts moved to Stodt Mountain in 1953; registers list the site as gone.

facts.design: Pole L-4 tower per FFLOS; a 1942 inspector's letter describes a 60-foot log tower with a 14x14 cabin
facts.status_note: Removed in 1953; cab or structure went to Stodt Mountain per sources that disagree on how much; FFLOS and firelookout.com say gone

staffing.status: occupied by a couple living in the cabin

events.note: Constructed in 1934 per ORWW; weebly also quotes a 1934 'lookout tower constructed' entry. Other entries give a November 1936 raising and a build about 1937
Activated March 9, 1942 under the Eugene Filter Center; May 5, 1942 visit found a man and wife living in the cabin
Cab moved to Stodt Lookout (FFLOS); tower relocated to Stodt Mountain (ORWW); structure dismantled and parts salvaged (weebly)
Registered November 16, 2010; nominated by Ray Kresek

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS says the 1930s; ORWW and a 1934 weebly entry say 1934; a November 1936 entry says the tower was framed and raised, and a 1942 inspector's letter says built about 1937. The story uses 1934 and lists the other dates.
FFLOS calls it a pole L-4 tower; the 1942 inspector's letter describes a 60-foot log tower with a 14x14 cabin. The brief's 18.3 m height follows the 60-foot figure.

FFLOS says the cab moved to Stodt Lookout; ORWW says the tower was relocated; the weebly history says the structure was dismantled and salvaged parts used. The Stodt register says its own cab and cables came from other Lincoln FPA towers, so the sources do not settle what came from South Beaver.
FFLOS gives 539 ft (164 m), which matches the brief's 164.3 m; firelookout.com and ORWW give 518 ft.

notes_for_editor: Dates and tower type disagree across the four lookout histories; the story says so. No notable fires appear in any source read. The brief's Western Lane FPA agency is from FFLOS only; the weebly page names the Siuslaw National Forest and a Lincoln FPA annual report. Nothing in the sources describes the site today. Stodt Mountain (FFLOS US 740) is a separate former site and was not researched here.
